state.seed_assertion: When a technician identifies a defect but does not immediately repair it, the finding should be recorded as an open next action rather than written as a resolved maintenance event.

sentences.1: When a technician identifies a defect but does not immediately repair it, the finding should be recorded as an open next action rather than written as a resolved maintenance event.
sentences.2: If a technician notices a leak but does not repair it, record the finding as an open next action.
sentences.3: Do not write it as though the maintenance event resolved the issue.
sentences.4: Maintenance logs should include recurring faults in analysis to identify when a repair has not resolved the underlying issue.
sentences.5: If a machine fails once, you repair it.
sentences.6: If it fails the same way repeatedly, your log should force a different conversation.
sentences.7: The manual has a note on that GSV that is easy to walk past: include the WALLCLOCKTIME GSV in only one user task, or wrap it in a UID/UIE pair if another task also reads it.
sentences.8: Possible causes include a forced-off condition in the program, an incorrect I/O tree mapping after a module replacement, or a faulted slot that has been inhibited.
